gap: No result ChatGPT got prices the shunt-meter category side by side today: the same class of 500 A, 10–120 V screen meter with a 20 ft cable sells for $79.99 at Vatrer, $87.99 at Renogy (ChatGPT's pick), $89.99 at LiTime and $92.99 at Redodo, while LiTime's $56.99 RS485 display (not the $59.99 ChatGPT showed) works only with three LiTime 51.2 V GC Comm batteries.
standout_why: I compared against cartvoltage.com/best-lithium-battery-meter-golf-cart (cited), cartvoltage.com/golf-cart-battery-meter-wrong-lithium (top result) and ChatGPT's own answer. Cartvoltage gives no prices at all, only 'Check Price on Amazon' links, and covers just the Junctek KG140F, Renogy 500A, Victron SmartShunt and the pack's own app. It already states the Victron 6.5–70 V limit and that the Renogy's Bluetooth is an add-on. Neither page names the Vatrer, LiTime or Redodo 500A screen meters or their prices. ChatGPT's answer said the LiTime display is 'excellent for compatible LiTime batteries' but did not name the three models it works with or that LiTime says it works with no other brand, and its $59.99 price is $3 above LiTime's store today.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's split: a shunt meter with a screen for any brand of pack (36/48/72 V) and Victron only up to 48 V. It changes the price advice. Renogy's $87.99 meter is not the cheapest of its kind: Vatrer's 500A shunt meter is $79.99 today. The Redodo 500A meter ($92.99), which ships inside our Redodo 48V 100Ah kit, is the dearest bought on its own. The LiTime display ($56.99) is the cheapest way to read real BMS charge, but only if the cart has a LiTime 51.2V 30Ah GC2 Comm, 60Ah GC Comm or 100Ah GC Comm battery. Vatrer's $89.99 10–90 V touchscreen meter is likewise tied to Vatrer Bluetooth batteries, which suits buyers of our Vatrer 48V 105Ah kit.
